text:
Match each item in Column A with its description in Column B.
Column A
(1) decision variables
(2) an infeasible region
(3) an unbounded feasible region
(4) a bounded feasible region
Column B
(a) The unknowns whose values are chosen to reach the best objective value.
(b) A feasible region that stretches without limit in some direction.
(c) The area outside the feasible region, where at least one constraint fails.
(d) A feasible region that can be enclosed in a circle.

points.text: (1) decision variables goes with (a).
(2) an infeasible region goes with (c).
(3) an unbounded feasible region goes with (b).
(4) a bounded feasible region goes with (d).

Column A

(d) A point that satisfies all the constraints of a problem.

points.text: (1) an optimal feasible solution goes with (c).
(2) an infeasible solution goes with (a).
(3) a feasible solution goes with (d).
(4) optimisation goes with (b).

text:
Match each item in Column A with its description in Column B.
Column A
(1) constraints
(2) a linear programming problem
(3) a corner point
(4) the feasible region
Column B
(a) The linear inequalities or equations that the variables of a problem must satisfy.
(b) The set of points satisfying all the constraints of the problem.
(c) A point where the boundary lines of the feasible region meet.
(d) A problem of finding the maximum or minimum of a linear function, under linear constraints.

points.text: (1) constraints goes with (a).
(2) a linear programming problem goes with (d).
(3) a corner point goes with (c).
(4) the feasible region goes with (b).
